- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., +0.10 to +0.30), model underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% per sentiment unit.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model often fails to reflect it — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of negative trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates near-term (first 5–7 days) — apply 2–3% downward bias to early forecast points.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate — apply 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
